t: Pakistan was created on 14 August 1947 by the partition of British India, in riots that killed between 200,000 and 2,000,000 people and the largest migration in history; it adopted a republican constitution in 1956 and became an Islamic republic of two provinces, East and West Pakistan.

East Pakistan seceded as Bangladesh in 1971 after a nine-month war in which independent researchers estimate 300,000 to 500,000 civilians died; the loss drove Pakistan to build the nuclear weapons it tested in 1998, the seventh state to do so.
Military coups in 1958, 1977 and 1999 put generals in power for three long stretches, and the first transfer from one elected government to another came only in May 2013.
dyk: The name Pakistan was coined in January 1933 by the activist Choudhry Rahmat Ali in a pamphlet, Now or Never, as an acronym of Panjab, Afghania, Kashmir, Sindh and Baluchistan; in Persian and Urdu it also means 'the land of the pure'.
ev: Pakistan adopts a republican constitution and becomes an Islamic republic with two geographically separate provinces, East Pakistan and West Pakistan.
President Iskander Mirza imposes martial law and is succeeded by General Ayub Khan, who suspends the constitution; a presidential constitution follows in 1962.
After the military refuses to transfer power to the Awami League and launches Operation Searchlight, war with India ends in defeat and East Pakistan becomes Bangladesh.
A military coup against Zulfikar Ali Bhutto's Pakistan Peoples Party ends democracy; General Zia-ul-Haq becomes president in 1978 and Islamises law and the economy.
Nawaz Sharif authorises nuclear tests in answer to India's, making Pakistan the seventh nuclear-armed state.
The Kargil War brings Pakistan and India to the brink, and General Pervez Musharraf takes power in a bloodless coup.
After Benazir Bhutto's assassination in 2007 the Pakistan Peoples Party wins the election; Musharraf resigns on 18 August and Asif Ali Zardari succeeds him.
The Pakistan Muslim League (N) wins the general election and Nawaz Sharif becomes prime minister for the third time, in the first successful democratic transition.

f.founder: Muhammad Ali Jinnah, founder of Pakistan and its first governor-general; the republic of 1956 succeeded the dominion he had led
f.predecessor: Dominion of Pakistan (1947–1956), a monarchy within the Commonwealth created by the partition of British India
